text:
tala: heads-up  I pushed phoenix-mini-int6 to staging (canary 12%) and the multilingual short-query holdout (<=18 tokens) shows an odd Recall@3 gap vs our onboard baseline. noticed it on the daily heatmap. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

ops-bot: deploy complete  phoenix-mini-int6 -> staging (canary 12%). dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/staging/models/phoenix-mini/variants/int6

hiro: re-ran a quick KNN eval against the canary for the short-holdout set. command:
```bash
./eval/run_knn.sh --model phoenix-mini-int6 --queries holdout/short_multilang.json --k 3 --seed 101
```
snippet:
```text
Recall@3: 0.63
Baseline (harbor-v1): 0.72
Churn@3: 0.18
```

samir: quick per-lang micro-breakdown (N=800 each):
```text
lang  baseline  phoenix-int6  delta
en    0.74      0.71          -0.03
es    0.70      0.58          -0.12
ja    0.69      0.56          -0.13
```

meera: that looks like subword-heavy langs losing neighbors. phoenix-mini-int6 used the new 6-bit per-tensor quant config from quant-pipeline-2.0. we have phoenix-mini-int8_pc built but not trafficed.

tala: can we flip a routing rule in staging to try int8_pc for short queries of ES/JA without redeploy? want to test quickly before wider rollout.

devex-bot: yes. example commands:
```bash
redwood model set-variant --model phoenix-mini --variant int8_pc --traffic 8 --env staging
redwood route add-rule --model phoenix-mini --condition "tokens <= 18 and lang in [\"es\",\"ja\"]" --variant int8_pc --env staging
```

hiro: applied int8_pc 8% + routing rule. re-ran the same eval on the int8_pc slice. results:
```text
Recall@3: 0.69
Baseline (harbor-v1): 0.72
Churn@3: 0.09
es delta: -0.04
ja delta: -0.03
```

samir: better but still a slight gap. also computed cosine-diff hist between harbor-v1 and phoenix-int8_pc on 2k anchors — mean drop ~0.02, but tails in ES/JA show bigger shifts (~0.08).

meera: two actionables: 1) run a 10k stratified short eval overnight comparing int6/int8_pc/harbor-v1 and capture NN-lists + cosine hist + id-flip rate, 2) check post-processing parity (centering/whitening) — I remember harbor-v1 uses small PCA whitening that onboarding scripts sometimes forget.

tala: agreed. adding a quick whitening parity check now. devex-bot can toggle postproc flags w/o redeploy?

devex-bot: yes. example:
```bash
redwood postproc set --model phoenix-mini --whiten true --center true --env staging
```

hiro: toggled whitening+center for phoenix-mini-int8_pc slice and re-ran a small 1k test. numbers now:
```text
Recall@3 (int8_pc + whiten): 0.71
Baseline: 0.72
Churn@3: 0.06
es delta: -0.02
ja delta: -0.01
```

samir: whitening recovered most of the gap. p95 latency impact negligible (+2ms). overnight large-run scheduled. I'll drop artifacts to RED-4102 when done.

meera: rollout suggestion based on today:
- keep phoenix-mini-int6 for long queries (>64 tokens) for cost reasons
- route short ES/JA queries (<=18 tokens) to phoenix-mini-int8_pc for 24h canary at 25% traffic with whitening enabled
- monitor Recall@3 per-lang, Churn@3, id-flip rate, and cosine-drift; alert if recall delta > 0.03 absolute
- run synthetic suffix perturbation tests to detect brittle subword behavior

tala: I'll open RED-4102 with commands, eval commands, and the checklist. scheduling 15m sync tomorrow 09:45 PT to review overnight. tagging @sre for rollback playbook if latency or errors spike. thanks all :thumbsup:
